title: Is Your Website AI-Search Ready? Here’s How to Tell
author: Ahaan Software
content:
Imagine your website ticks all the boxes with an ideal UI/UX design, SEO-optimised content, and performance that is unbeatable – yet your website gains no traction. With a digitally evolving landscape, making your mark is no longer simply about your web design but about a site that adapts to AI. Artificial intelligence continues to redefine how users connect with businesses, and with AI-powered searches, visibility has become a competition.  

Keep your website future-proof and optimise your business for AI-powered searches that rely on structured algorithms to identify the top websites. In this blog, we’ll explore how AI dominates search engines and how to build a website that tops AI-search rankings. 

 

The Growing Trend of AI-Search 

In 2023, nearly 13 million users were estimated to use AI as their primary search tool, and by 2027, a staggering number of over 90 million Americans are projected to primarily use AI search engines. AI search engines like ChatGPT, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot, and Google’s Search Generative Experience are rapidly changing how users discover information and businesses online.  

Unlike SERP, AI models recognise trusted sites with reliable information, fast speed, and optimised content. While AI searches will not be replacing SERP soon, users tend to rely on top-generated results for their informational needs. 

 

Signs That Your Website is AI-Search Ready 

Most business owners think that being AI-ready translates to mastering ChatGPT; however, in reality, that is far from true. Stay ahead of your competitors and design a website that appears at the top by keeping up with digital trends and AI algorithms.  

Is your website ready to dominate AI searches? Let’s find out: 

  1. Structured and Technical Content 

Your website should have clear and structured content that is legible by both AI and humans. A technical structure is important so AI models can easily access and interpret it. A hierarchical structure with appropriate headings, meta-tags, and schema markups keeps your website updated in AI search results.  

  1. Optimised Speed and Responsiveness 

Just like humans, AI search engines aren’t patient and recommend websites that keep the flow going. If your website blends together speed, performance, and responsiveness, you’re already on the way to being seen on AI user searches.  

  1. AI-Indexing Optimised Content 

Create content that isn’t simply decorative but also informative. Smart and modern tools like AI searches are built to recognise content that is authoritative and written with expertise. If short paragraphs, strong keywords, and clear headings sound like your website, you’re already on the way to future-proofing your site.  

 

How to Optimise Your Website for AI-Powered Searches 

With the launch of Google’s AI Search in 2024, it was expected that the organic traffic of websites would go down by 18-64%. In such a new and challenging digital ecosystem, it’s important to align a site to evolving practices with measures that optimise AI searches: 

  • Focus on content that is high-quality and authoritative. 
  • Use long-tail and semantic keywords for best SEO aligned to AI searches. 
  • Optimise your website not just for technical SEO but also for speed, mobile responsiveness, and user experience with structured data schemas.  
  • Build a strong social media presence to help AI identify, connect, and gather holistic insights for the best search results.  
  • Be up to date with SEO audits to adapt website strategies to changes in AI search algorithms.  

 

Practices to Avoid for Best AI Results 

Still relying on SERP models for your website will only decrease your website’s visibility. For example, while SERP models are trained to identify target keywords, AI models target keywords that are elaborative. As Google Senior Vice President and Chief Business Officer said, “The volume of searches with five or more words grew 1.5x as fast as shorter queries.”   

Traversing through digital changes requires you to be updated – and with AI searches, replacing old practices with a renewed understanding of how AI searches work is essential.  

  • Ditch the keyword dumping and choose content that is natural and conversational.  
  • Avoid a UI/UX design that is slow, outdated, and redundant. 
  • Poor schema markup will only decrease the traffic on your site.  
  • Remove any AI blockers or restrictions from your website.  

 

Stay Ahead with a Website That Evolves with AI 

Your website is the most powerful asset for your business, and in today’s evolving digital landscape, it is important to make sure your brand is future-proof. Adapting to AI has not only become an advantage but also a necessity to keep your company thriving, especially in the digital ecosystem.  

By following best SEO and AI algorithm practices, optimise your website and appear at the top of AI searches across platforms.

title: Top 6 CMS Platforms to Power Your Small Business Website
author: Ahaan Software
content:
Running a small business and want to get your website up and running without spending a fortune on web developers? The best part is, in 2025, you no longer need to be a tech wizard to build a website for your business. With Content Management Systems (CMS), designing, managing, and growing a site for your business is a cakewalk.  

In this blog, we’ll break down the top 6 CMS options for small businesses to simplify web development, keep it budget-friendly, and create a site that truly works for your business.  

 

Why is a CMS necessary for my small business? 

A strong online presence matters – not just for your business, but for sustained growth and sales. Nearly 70% of small and medium-sized businesses utilise Content Management Systems to grow their website.  

Whether your business is on the lookout for a simple static website or a more creative flow of complex designs, CMS helps build the perfect website for you and your business without the cost of an expensive developer.  

With CMS, you can add new information, update your website, refurbish your layout, and give your website a makeover – all without knowing how to code. What CMS does is make your job easy by designing an all-in-one space where you can manage, modify, and grow through a site.  

 

Top 6 CMS For Small to Thriving Businesses 

As of 2025, there are more than 82 million live websites across the internet designed through CMS. For small businesses, building a customer base and scaling growth is essential – with these 7 best Content Management Systems, choose a setup that works for you and your brand.  

  • WordPress 

The most popular website platform, WordPress, is worth 62.7% of the CMS market share and is used by popular organisations like PlayStation, Time Magazine, The Rolling Stone, and Meta Newsroom.  

Pros: 

  1. User-friendly setup 
  1. Ready-to-use website templates 
  2. Extensive library of plugins  
  3. Free plans available 

Cons: 

  1. Difficult to manage complex content 
  2. Requires regular updates 
  • Shopify 

If selling products online is your target, Shopify is the best way to go. As the name suggests, this CMS platform is built for users who want to shop and businesses that want to sell.  

In 2024, there were over 3.9 million live websites developed and managed through Shopify. With a focus on e-commerce stores, Shopify hosts multi-channel tools with an app marketplace.  

Pros: 

  1. Unlimited products on all plans 
  2. Powerful e-commerce features with multiple sales channels 
  3. Supports 100+ payment gateways alongside an in-house solution 

Cons: 

  1. Paid subscription plans starting at ₹1,499/month for the Basic Plan 
  2. Higher transaction fees for payments on third-party platforms 
  3. Limited blogging functionality 
  • Squarespace  

If you own a portfolio-based small business, Squarespace is the best space for you. For all artists, photographers, and boutique stores, Squarespace provides modern templates with a neat design to help you sell, showcase, and blog your work effortlessly with stunning visual appeal. 

Pros:  

  1. Professional and visually appealing designs 
  2. Built-in analytics 
  3. Top image quality and management 

Cons: 

  1. Paid (but all-inclusive) plans, starting at $23/month for businesses 
  2. Fewer options for third-party integrations 
  3. Steeper learning curve due to complex designs 
  • Wix 

One of the most widely used CMS platforms, Wix is a cloud-based system with a user-friendly drag-and-drop interface that is perfect for small businesses. Whether you own a restaurant business or want to show off your portfolio, Wix is the way to go with over 500+ customisable templates, filtered by industry.  

Pros: 

  1. Extensive SEO tools and free hosting 
  2. Highly mobile responsive designs 
  3. App marketplace and e-commerce capabilities 
  4. Free plan available with limited features 

Cons: 

  1. Limited customisation 
  2. Does not support migration to other platforms 
  3. High long-term subscription costs  
  • Joomla 

A large marketplace with endless templates and extensions, Joomla helps you build websites that match your needs. Joomla serves as the perfect middle ground between complex platforms and extremely simple platforms, making it a space for every small business owner. Whether you’re looking to start from scratch or integrate CRM into your site, Joomla does it all.  

Pros: 

  1. Free and open-source  
  2. Advanced user management systems with multilingual support 
  3. Extensive APIs and strong security networks for sensitive data 
  4. Structured data handling with built-in features 

Cons: 

  1. Smaller marketplace extension 
  2. Steeper learning curve for beginners 
  3. Needs more technical knowledge to operate 
  • Drupal 

If you’re looking for a highly secure and flexible platform for complex content structures that scales extensively with you, Drupal is the CMS solution you’ve been waiting for. It has an extensive set of advanced features and robust capabilities that make it ideal for small businesses, which come with high demands and requirements.  

Pros: 

  1. High-level security networks with strong protection against data breaches 
  2. High performance and scalability  
  3. Advanced content structures for intricate content management and best UI/UX 

Cons: 

  1. Steep learning curve with developer assistance needed 
  2. Higher implementation and subscription costs 
  3. Fewer ready-to-use templates and design options 

How to Choose the Right CMS for Your Business? 

Just like choosing the right physical location can boost your sales by 200%, the CMS platform you choose can either elevate or slow down your business. Take the smarter route and go beyond generic recommendations to choose a CMS platform that does wonders for your site in just one click: 

  • Budget:  

Consider not just the one-time cost, but the long-term expenses you will be investing in the CMS to maintain your site. 

  • Ease of Use:  

If you’re not an expert technician or don’t have a team of web developers, it is ideal to choose a CMS whose UI/UX is easy to use and simple. 

  • Scalability:  

If you have to migrate to another CMS to accommodate your growth, it makes no sense. Choose a CMS that is built with scalability in mind.  

  • Customisation:  

Every business is unique, and your CMS should incorporate design freedom, customisation, and flexible plugin support.  

  • Business Type:  

A small business doesn’t always mean a retail shop, and you should choose a CMS that is compatible with your business type. If you’re into retail sales, platforms like Shopify are ideal, but if you’re a portfolio-based business, it’s recommended to use platforms like Wix.  

Grow Your Small Business with the Content Management Systems 

Building a website for your small business does not need to be complex or expensive. With the right CMS, design and manage a site that grows your online presence without making things more complicated.  

Choose from the top 6 CMS and align your business goals to a system that understands how to bring your business vision to life.

title: What Makes a Great Homepage 5 Key Features You Need
author: Ahaan Software
content:
When you walk into a store, the initial layout creates an impression that drives your motivation to shop; that is exactly what the homepage of your website does for you. Driving online presence in today’s abundance of e-commerce is difficult, so if a customer visits your website, it is important that your homepage reflects your brand identity and guides them to stay.  

In this blog, we’ll decode what exactly makes a homepage great and the top 5 features to keep your homepage attractive, relevant and the focus of driving sales.  

What Makes a Great Homepage? 

Reports show that users usually leave a website within the first 10-20 seconds, so it is up to businesses to design a homepage that retains users and converts visits to sales with clarity, purpose, and style.  

Consider your homepage as the doorstep to your digital store – one that either sets the impression or turns the customer away. Essentially, a great homepage captures the user’s attention, communicates the value your brand adds, and guides them to the next step.  

User experience is the key, and with a great homepage, welcome your customer into a website that feels more like an experience rather than simply browsing. Balance form and function with a great homepage that is designed keeping the customer in mind. 

5 Key Features Every Great Homepage Must Have 

The homepage is possibly the most important page on your website, and cracking the key to designing a great webpage is essential to scaling your business. Most businesses lose out on value because they don’t pay attention to how necessary design is – stay ahead of the noise and incorporate these 5 elements to make your homepage stand out to not only users but also your competitors.  

  1. Easy Access and Navigation 

Your homepage is the key to your website – one that should be welcoming and accessible for your customers. Design a homepage that orients your customers to your business and interlinks itself to other pages across your website through implicit and explicit links. Include clear and distinctive link labels so users know what each interlinked page stands for, and make navigation easy.  

Make sure to place your primary navigation toolbar, preferably at the top or at an accessible location on your homepage, so users can explore your website without getting frustrated. Decrease user bounce rates with a page design that not only loads fast, can be easily located, and offers a clear path from the homepage, but is also mobile responsive.  

Pro Tip: Include a search box in the navigation bar for best results.  

  1. Clarity in Communication through Content 

Your website has 10 seconds to crack the deal, so treat your homepage as the elevator pitch and get straight to business from the get-go. 38% of users reportedly stop engaging with a website if its content is unattractive. Use not only high-quality imagery but also top-notch content to keep users interested.  

A homepage tagline that conveys what you do without spelling it out is exactly what smart and engaging communication is – leverage it to build your business’s value proposition. Today, users rarely read what your page says; rather, they scan – design your homepage with content, imagery, and logos that convey the message in one go.  

  1. Establish Trustworthiness through Examples 

Don’t just tell, but rather show the work you do. Your homepage is responsible not only for drawing customers in but also for giving them a reason to stay. What better way to build a network of customers than to establish trust in the first 10 seconds?  

Your page fold is the most crucial part of your homepage – utilise the space to show numbers and display the work you’ve done. Use a responsive design to display content from other pages within your site to build a network of interlinking for a better ranking. Add an RSS to keep users updated on new content, especially if your webpage works in the blogging or news industry. 

  1. Strategic and Clear Call-to-Actions 

Incorporating an engaging banner on your homepage is non-negotiable to not only convey important messages but also encourage a CTA that can change your entire gameplay. Your CTA shouldn’t be lengthy and long but rather have very few words that show rather than tell.  

The placement of your CTA buttons is equally important and should ideally be above the fold or at the top right corner to catch the user’s attention. Both primary and secondary calls to action are important, especially on your homepage, to attract users to explore and dig deeper into the work you do.  

  1. Simple and User-Friendly 

The main purpose of your homepage is to drive engagement and not confuse users. While some websites may work better with a high technical language, most businesses, news sites, and blogging platforms will generate a high user responsiveness with a simple and user-friendly interface.  

Avoid long paragraphs and stick to brevity that not only conveys the message but also avoids making your site look like a textbook. However, simple doesn’t mean boring – ditch the standard templates, and design a homepage that stands out and blends in animations, colours, and texts to create an experience for your users. Strike the perfect balance between a simple UI/UX and a rich exploration experience.  

Pro Tip: While an experiential design can crack the code for you, it’s best not to go overboard and create a complex layout that decreases user interaction for a general audience.  

Design a Homepage That Makes Users Stay 

As web design continues to evolve, your homepage becomes more and more crucial for user retention. Optimise the potential in how your homepage looks, speaks, and shows your brand to customers for unmatched growth and success.  

Use these 5 key strategies to tap into how a customer views your site, and design a homepage UI/UX that makes them want to keep scrolling.

title: Top 5 Ways to Boost Your Online Store Speed for Best Customer Interaction
author: Ahaan Software
content:
If you’re walking into a retail store, you walk in with expectations of a speedy, seamless, and smooth purchase that leaves you with a shopping experience worth remembering. The same goes for an online store. In e-commerce, nothing matters more than speed; a website that takes forever to load will turn away customers before they even get to your products.  

In this blog, we’ll unpack why speed is crucial in e-commerce success and how to increase the speed of your website for improved SERP ranking and a customer experience that keeps users coming back.  

Why Does Your E-Store’s Speed Matter? 

Did you know that sites with a loading speed of 1 second have a bounce rate of 7%, while an increase to a 5-second response speed results in a 38% bounce rate? In a world that runs on time as currency, as an e-commerce store, you can’t afford delays. With nearly 70% of consumers making a purchase choice based on website loading time, you can’t afford to build a website that does everything right but fails in performance.  

Your page speed not only impacts your SERP rankings but also impacts your Core Web Vitals score. By improving your page performance through fast speed, you not only improve customer experience but also drive traffic and scalability to your online business. In simple words, what a faster website does for you is make your online store pop up first, drive users, convert them to happy customers, and ultimately scale your business to success.  

Top 5 Ways to Boost Your Website Speed 

Your online store is the gateway to your e-commerce business and should tick all the boxes to keep customers happy and returning for repeated purchases. With these powerful methods, boost your success by supercharging your online page – 

  1. Choose the right CMS 

A right Content Management System (CMS) determines the amount of traffic, load, and engagement you bring to your website. Choose the right platform based on your business type – if you’re an online store that simply deals in selling products, Shopify is your go-to platform; however, for visual-heavy brands that blend portfolio with sales, Wix might be the better choice.  

Different CMS platforms have different website speeds based on your design, content, and traffic size – make a smart choice by aligning your needs to the CMS speed.  

  1. Optimize your website content 

It isn’t simply your website platform that determines performance speed, but also your theme. With speed testing tools, choose a theme with fast-loading elements and optimized images that are lightweight.  

Compress your images and videos for quick loading and access without slowing down your entire site. Reduce any misdirects or broken links that slow down your website, and minimize third-party extensions for a faster loading interface.  

  1. Implement lazy loading  

Why wait for your entire webpage to load when you can be smart and keep your user engaged? With lazy loading, your website will focus on loading the content that is visible on the screen first, instead of loading the entire webpage content together.  

Use this performance optimization technique to reduce resource consumption and drive the server bandwidth for the best speed.  

  1. Improve mobile e-commerce loading responsiveness 

While your business may have the fastest desktop website, what it’s missing is a mobile webpage that doesn’t disappoint. Nearly 1.65 billion people globally shop on their mobile phones, and a slow mobile website will only hinder your growth.  

Use Accelerated Mobile Pages (AMP) to improve how your online store handles traffic and loads on mobile phones. From optimizing images and enabling browser caching to choosing a mobile-responsive theme, it is crucial to work on a responsive mobile online store to cater to a wider range of user experiences.  

  1. Use a Content Delivery Network (CDN) 

What a CDN essentially does is bring a network of servers that contain your website data so that the user can easily access the data from the server closest to them. By using CDN, you reduce the time it takes for your online store’s content to load and distribute traffic evenly.  

Top Ways to Measure Your Online Store’s Speed 

Simply boosting your page speed isn’t enough–it’s equally important to track your online store’s performance to make sure your page is delivering consistent speed. With these tools, stay at the top of your game and reap all the benefits that a supercharged website has to offer: 

  • Google PageSpeed website:  

With PageSpeed Insights, get a free report of your online store’s speed and performance and identify areas of strength and improvement.  

  • GTMetrix:  

Check your page loading speed across various devices and locations to know if your site starts slowing down. This site offers key metrics across the loading speed of images, scripts, stylesheets, and other elements to test how fast your website performs.  

  • Pingdom:  

Whether it is page loading speed, uptime, or simply performance metrics, Pingdom pings you with all important updates to boost your website’s traffic in the form of a detailed report. It additionally offers real-time monitoring so you can troubleshoot your site’s speed immediately.  

Ready to Speed Your Way to E-commerce Success? 

Whether you’re looking to build a new website or targeting Shopify speed optimization, the importance of performance and speed in e-commerce is undeniable. Upgrade your website to the next level with pages that load immediately to give your customers an unmatched experience.  

With a website that has lightning speed, you not only win customers but also build trust and success.

title: The Beginner’s Guide to Building a Modern Website in 2025 (No Coding Needed!)
author: Ahaan Software
content:
Have you always wanted to build a website from scratch, but the fear of coding kept you at a halt? In 2025, designing a website is no longer reserved for developers, but a majority of websites are built without code.  

Whether you’re starting a small business, building an online portfolio, or digitally documenting your life on the Internet, creating a modern website has never been easier, especially if you’re a newbie.

With powerful no-code modern website builders, creating a site no longer requires expertise in technology and coding, but simply an idea to begin.  

Checklist for Designing a Modern Website (Without Coding) 

Whether you plan to launch your website within a few days or plan to patiently build it over weeks, the basic checklist of designing a modern website is simple: 

  1. Planning your website

  1. Developing a web design and template 
  • Choose an appropriate web theme or template that is readily available and customizable. 
  • Define a colour palette and font for your website to maintain branding and tonality that is consistent with your purpose. 
  • Create essential webpages within your website, such as a homepage, about page, and different pages for your content.  
  1. Testing and launching 
  • Check the functionality of all elements on your website, including links, buttons, and additional elements.

What Features Makes Your Website Modern?

Building a Website Has Never Been Easier – Start Today! 

Don’t let the fear of technology stop you from getting a custom-built website. Today, technology has evolved adequately, and designing a website is a cakewalk. Whether you’re a beginner who wants to create a modern website with AI or you’re getting started after a hiatus, let your creativity take over and build a modern website that skyrockets you to success.

title: Augmented Reality Trends for Online Retail in 2026
author: Ahaan Software
content:
With a global e-commerce market of $4.8 trillion, it becomes difficult to find a unique selling point that makes your online retail store stand out. Don’t be just another website in the SERP list, but create a unique shopping experience for your customers with Augmented Reality (AR) online retail.  

Offer your shoppers an engaging platform where your online store transforms into a virtual space for them to interact with your products and enjoy an unmatched experience.  

In this blog, we’ll decode how Augmented Reality (AR) is ready to shape the digital landscape of 2025 and how you can stay on top by following key trends.  

Augmented Reality in Online Retail Explained 

Whether you’re shopping for a bookshelf to keep in your living room or the perfect lipstick to match a new dress, the number one pain point in online shopping is being unable to physically see or try on the product. This is exactly what AR solves.  

Augmented Reality (AR) bridges the gap between the physical and the digital by harnessing technology to generate a richer user experience through an immersive digital environment. From virtually trying on clothes to visualizing a paint shade in your bedroom, AR overlays digital content onto your real-world stimuli through both websites and mobile phones.  

How AR is Set to Revolutionize E-commerce in 2026 

Globally, the AR market is projected to reach USD 46.6 billion in 2025, and with every passing day, more and more online shopping platforms are incorporating augmented reality online retail strategies in their game plan.  

The shift in consumer preferences since the pandemic has brought augmented reality to the center of e-commerce in the future. From being able to virtually try on clothes, visualize furniture in your house, or even see how accessories look on you, with augmented reality, the digital space becomes the customer’s reality, and they’re no longer left wondering whether the product they’ve purchased is the right choice. 

Key AR Trends Shaping Online Retail 

The future of AR in e-commerce is highly profitable – with these key trends, transform your online retail platform with Augmented Reality to design a future-forward store: 

  • Trend 1: WebAR integration 

By integrating AR onto your website, your consumers can enjoy a seamless product interaction without the hassle of downloading an app.  

  • Trend 2: AR-powered smart glasses  

With this wearable hardware technology, shop-on-the-go becomes easier, allowing your customers to project digital content in the real world.  

  • Trend 3: Real-time AR product customization. 

If your customers are trying on a product but need customizations, don’t let that be a hindrance. Opt for AR product customization, so your shoppers can instantly modify and customize products in size, shape, color, and design for the best satisfaction.  

  • Trend 4: Integration with social commerce (Instagram, TikTok, etc.) 

Increase your brand’s visibility by integrating AR with your e-commerce store on social media (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, etc.). Let your shoppers experience virtual try-on as a feature when scrolling through different products and ease the purchase process.  

  • Trend 5: Virtual AR showrooms  

Don’t let your customers be confused about making a purchase, especially for high-value products. Instead, integrate virtual AR showrooms on your online retail page so they can feel your digital products being displayed in real-time scenarios and make a sound choice.  

Top Benefits of AR in E-Shopping Experience 

If you’re still not convinced about integrating Augmented Reality Online Retail, take a look at the top benefits that are driving brands like Apple, Google, and IKEA to adopt AR practices in their everyday shopping culture: 

  • Conversion rates increase by up to 94% with AR-enabled products. 
  • 71% of consumers are more likely to purchase a product from an AR-integrated website.  
  • AR helps shoppers visualize products more accurately, leading to 25–40% fewer returns. 
  • Data reports that AR eCommerce experiences are 200% more engaging than non-AR shopping experiences.  

Shape the Future of Online Shopping with Augmented Reality  

Despite customers demanding Augmented Reality in their online shopping experience, only 15% of retailers have incorporated it. Seize the opportunity and technologically upgrade your shopping website to make your customers feel heard.  

With the future of online retail slowly shifting towards an Augmented Reality landscape, explore key trends and bridge the gap between the physical reality and the digital world.  

Ready to upgrade your store experience? Explore AR tools that fit your platform.

title: How Digital Presence Builds Business Reputation

content:

What Is Digital Presence Really? 

Recent data shows that 97% of people review a company’s online presence before deciding to visit their business or make a purchase. Digital presence isn’t simply a trend turned bandwagon that top businesses are jumping on; it is about being visible, consistent, and active.

The way your business appears on digital platforms is how your company’s digital presence is built as a storefront that is available 24/7.  

In current times, strengthening your business’s digital presence doesn’t only mean being listed, but also having a comprehensive digital strategy. Whether it is posting regularly, interacting with your audience, or growing with user-generated content, platforms like LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, and YouTube keep you and your brand relevant with customers and offer them a space to address concerns and answer queries.

With SEO, change how frequently your business appears on the search engine. By implementing search engine optimization, you make your content accessible for search engines like Google, who in turn make it highly visible to AI searches as well as manual searches, to connect your business with the right audience.  

With the right SEO strategies, such as high-value keywords and a consistent NAP, push your website, especially on local searches, to improve to a high ranking and optimize your digital presence for nearby customers.
